ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The picture is a schematic diagram of the life cycle of a beetle, with pink circular arrows connecting each stage. At the top there is a cluster of eggs, labeled B; on the right side and below there are grub-like larval stages, labeled A; at the lower left there is a light-colored, wrapped transitional stage, labeled C; on the left side is an adult beetle, labeled D. Reasoning: The question asks about the stage of a completely metamorphosing insect between larva and adult, which does not eat and completes transformation in a cocoon or hardened outer shell. Biologically, this stage is called pupa, namely a pupa. The light-colored wrapped stage in the picture located between larva and adult also corresponds to a pupa.
